findings: The candidate narrows “simplified shared_ptr” instead of pretending to implement the full standard-library type.
A single shared control block maintains the strong-count invariant across copy, move, assignment, reset and destruction.
Copy-and-swap avoids releasing old ownership before safely acquiring new ownership; move operations transfer the token without increasing the count.
The exact C++17 candidate is compiled with warnings-as-errors and independently exercises null ownership, copy/move/self-assignment, reset, 1000-copy fan-out and last-release destruction.
The concurrency and cyclic-reference limitations are explicit, preventing the teaching implementation from being misrepresented as production std::shared_ptr.
